title: The First-Principles Breaker
description: Strips any topic down to its most basic, jargon-free foundational truths
prompt:
Explain this topic from first principles: [topic].

Rules:
- Remove ALL jargon. If a technical term is unavoidable, define it immediately.
- Focus only on the core ideas that are absolutely necessary to understand the topic
- Start from what we know for certain, then build up
- If I can't understand this after reading your explanation, the explanation failed — not me
useCase: Deconstructing overwhelmingly complex systems into their most basic, undeniable foundational truths to ensure baseline comprehension.

title: The Fast Context Builder
description: Gives a high-level map of a subject so you know what to learn first and what can wait
prompt:
Give me a high-level overview of this subject: [subject].

Structure your response as:
1. What this subject is fundamentally about (2-3 sentences max)
2. The 4-5 most important ideas that connect everything
3. What I should learn FIRST (the foundation)
4. What I can learn LATER once the foundation is solid
5. One common misconception beginners have about this subject
useCase: Establishing a macro-level cognitive map before diving into granular, technical specifics that cause cognitive overload.

title: The Feynman Teacher
description: Makes you explain a topic in your own words, then pinpoints exactly where your understanding breaks down
prompt:
Ask me to explain this topic in my own words: [topic].

After I give my explanation:
1. Point out exactly where my explanation is unclear or logically incorrect
2. Identify any gaps — things I skipped that are actually critical
3. Tell me what I got right (specifically, not generically)
4. Re-explain only the parts I got wrong, as simply as possible

Do not let me get away with vague explanations. If I say 'it kind of works like...' push me to be precise.
useCase: Exposing hidden gaps in comprehension by forcing the learner to articulate concepts actively, revealing true understanding versus mere familiarity.

title: The Example Accelerator
description: Explains any concept through 3 tiered examples — simple, practical, and advanced
prompt:
Explain this concept using exactly 3 examples: [concept]

- Example 1 — Simple: Use the most everyday, relatable scenario possible. A child should understand this.
- Example 2 — Practical: Show how this concept applies in a real professional or academic context.
- Example 3 — Advanced: Show a complex, nuanced application that an expert would encounter.

Keep each example explanation under 4 sentences. No filler.
useCase: Bridging the gap between abstract theoretical frameworks and concrete, real-world application through tiered complexity.

title: The Memory Lock-In
description: Converts abstract concepts into sticky mnemonics, analogies, and visual hooks for long-term retention
prompt:
Help me lock this information into long-term memory: [topic or concept]

Provide:
1. A mnemonic device (acronym, rhyme, or pattern) for the key points
2. A powerful analogy that makes the concept instantly click
3. A visual mental image I can associate with this concept
4. One sentence that summarizes the entire concept in plain language

Keep everything concise. The goal is sticky memory, not comprehensive explanation.
useCase: Converting abstract, difficult-to-retain data points into sticky, highly memorable cognitive hooks.

title: The Rapid Test Loop
description: Quizzes you on any topic with gradually increasing difficulty and explains mistakes immediately
prompt:
Quiz me with 5 questions on this topic: [topic]

Rules:
- Start easy (Question 1-2: basic recall)
- Get progressively harder (Question 3-4: application)
- Final question should require synthesis or analysis (Question 5)
- After EACH of my answers: tell me if I'm right or wrong immediately
- If wrong: explain the correct answer in 2 sentences and move on
- If right: confirm briefly and move to the next question

Do not give me all 5 questions at once. Ask one at a time.
useCase: Confirming knowledge acquisition rapidly and continually to prevent the accidental memorization of incorrect data structures.

title: The 30-Day Fast Learning System
description: Builds a full month-long curriculum in 4 weekly phases — clarity, understanding, recall, application
prompt:
Create a 30-day fast learning plan for mastering: [subject or skill]

Break it into 4 weekly themes:
- Week 1: Clarity (understand what this subject is and its core structure)
- Week 2: Understanding (go deep on the most important concepts)
- Week 3: Recall (actively test and reinforce everything learned)
- Week 4: Application (use the knowledge on real problems)

For each week, give daily learning tasks that take under 30 minutes per day. Be specific — tell me exactly what to do each day, not just general advice.
useCase: Architecting a long-term, low-friction curriculum to master entirely new disciplines sequentially without experiencing burnout.

title: The Sectional Focus Drill
description: Breaks complex topics into sections and enforces mastery of each before moving to the next
prompt:
Break the following complex topic into 4-6 logical sections: [topic]

Then:
1. Start with Section 1 only
2. Ask me 3 questions about Section 1
3. Evaluate my answers
4. Do NOT move to Section 2 until I have demonstrated complete understanding of Section 1
5. If I fail any question, re-explain that specific concept and re-test

Tell me which section we are on and how many remain. Enforce strict sequential progression.
useCase: Preventing cognitive overwhelm by enforcing strict, linear progression through highly complicated subject matter.

title: The Blind-Spot Identifier
description: Ruthlessly audits your explanation to expose what you think you know but actually don't
prompt:
I will explain my current understanding of [topic]. Instead of praising my explanation:

1. Tell me what I am probably MISUNDERSTANDING based on what I said
2. Identify where my explanation is logically weak or imprecise
3. Tell me specifically if there are critical gaps I am unaware of
4. Point out any oversimplifications that would cause problems in real application

Do not validate a poor explanation to be polite. If my understanding has fundamental flaws, tell me directly.

My explanation: [write your explanation here]
useCase: Acting as a ruthless intellectual auditor that prevents the AI from smoothing over poor explanations with false validation.

title: The Meeting Notes Retrieval Test
description: Converts passive meeting notes into active problem-solving scenarios that test real comprehension
prompt:
Here are my notes from: [meeting name / date]

[Paste your notes here]

Instead of summarizing them, turn these notes into a Retrieval Test. Give me 5 'What if?' scenarios based on these notes that require me to:
- Apply the decisions made in the meeting to a new problem
- Think through second-order consequences of the decisions
- Identify what information is missing that would change the decision

Ask the scenarios one at a time. Evaluate my responses after each one.
useCase: Forcing professionals to apply passive meeting notes to active problem-solving scenarios, ensuring alignment on strategic decisions.

title: The RACE Framework Educator
description: Uses Role, Action, Context, Expectation to design highly targeted persona-driven educational modules
prompt: Role: You are a senior university lecturer. Action: Explain the architecture of a multi-agent AI system. Context: The audience is first-year computer science students. Expectation: Provide a step-by-step breakdown using concrete analogies, avoiding advanced mathematical notation.
useCase: Designing highly targeted, persona-driven educational modules with explicit role, action, context, and expectation.

title: The Zero-Shot to Few-Shot Transition
description: Forces the AI to adopt a highly specific structural pedagogy using 3 reference examples
prompt: Here are three examples of how I want complex topics explained (brief intro, bulleted list of components, real-world application). Now, using this exact format, explain [New Concept].
useCase: Forcing the AI to adopt a highly specific structural pedagogy using few-shot example data.

title: The Socratic Debunker
description: Guides you to discover logical flaws in your own thinking through the Socratic method — no direct answers
prompt: I will provide a statement containing a subtle technical fallacy. Act as a teacher and guide me through the Socratic method to help me discover the flaw in my own logic without directly giving me the answer.
useCase: Building deep critical thinking skills through guided failure rather than direct correction.

title: The AI-Powered Lexicon Translator
description: Translates dense academic paragraphs to 8th-grade English while preserving all factual accuracy
prompt: Translate the following dense academic paragraph into simple, conversational English. Maintain all factual accuracy but reduce the reading level to an 8th-grade standard.
useCase: Democratizing access to highly complex research materials for students at all comprehension levels.

title: The 'Explain the Fix' Educator
description: Turns debugging sessions into active learning by explaining why the code failed before fixing it
prompt: Review this broken code snippet. Do not just provide the correct code. First, explain why it failed, what underlying concept I misunderstood, and then provide the corrected snippet with inline comments.
useCase: Turning debugging sessions into active learning opportunities that correct underlying conceptual misunderstandings.

title: The System Prompt Context Setter
description: Profiles your knowledge level and goals before teaching — prevents generalized one-size-fits-all answers
prompt: You are an expert on [topic]. Before answering any questions, ask me 3 clarifying questions about my current knowledge level and specific goals so you can tailor your curriculum perfectly to my needs.
useCase: Preventing generalized answers by forcing the AI to profile the learner's knowledge level and goals first.

title: The Multi-Step Breakdown (Chaining)
description: Chunks complex lessons into sequential steps with explicit confirmation gates before proceeding
prompt: Step 1: Define the core terms of [topic]. Step 2: Explain how they interact. Step 3: Provide a real-world case study. Execute Step 1 now and wait for my confirmation before proceeding.
useCase: Preventing cognitive overload by chunking complex lessons into confirmed sequential steps.

title: The Token-Optimized Explainer
description: Delivers raw information with maximum density — bullets, zero pleasantries, minimum word count
prompt: Explain [topic]. Use maximum token optimization: use bullet points, eliminate all pleasantries, remove redundant context, and use absolute minimum word count to convey the facts.
useCase: Rapid information retrieval for advanced learners seeking raw factual data without explanatory padding.

title: The Reverse-Engineering Task Master
description: Gives a working example then removes 3 critical components for you to fill in and justify
prompt: Provide me with a fully functioning example of [topic or system]. Then, remove 3 critical components and ask me to fill in the blanks, explaining my reasoning for each.
useCase: Forcing active recall through intentional system breakage and component reconstruction.

title: The Algorithmic Complexity Tutor
description: Explains time and space complexity by tracing each loop and data structure to its Big O contribution
prompt: Explain the time and space complexity of the provided code. Break down exactly how each loop and data structure contributes to the Big O notation.
useCase: Translating abstract mathematical theory into concrete, line-by-line code complexity analysis.
